ai.description: Calotes paulus is a small agamid reaching 7 cm snout-vent length. It features a brownish body with a distinct black streak behind the eye and a prominent, serrated dorsal crest.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Calotes paulus* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, black, comma-shaped patch located just above the tympanum, which is absent in similar Indian species.
ai.habitat: *Calotes paulus* typically inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, often found at elevations ranging from 500 to 1,500 meters in the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: *Calotes paulus* is primarily diurnal, often seen basking on tree trunks or low vegetation to regulate its body temperature before actively foraging for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Calotes paulus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 2–6 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, spanning from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Calotes paulus* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting high-elevation evergreen forests and shola grasslands above 1,000 meters.
